exposure: Very advanced maternal age (45 years and older)
cohort: 626 singleton newborns born to mothers of very advanced maternal age (VAMA, 45 years and older) were compared to matched controls comprised of advanced maternal age (AMA) mothers and mothers between 20 and 35 years of age.
finding: Newborns of VAMA mothers were less likely to be exclusively breastfed during hospitalization and more likely to experience early transient hypoglycemia and special care unit admission, but did not exhibit significantly increased major neonatal morbidities.
